Somalia exports third consignment of 17 tons of bananas to Saudi Arabia
                 |
                  08 June 2020 22:15 
            
            
		
 
        
			MOGADISHU-  Somalia has this week exported 17 tons of bananas to Saudi Arabia and Turkey, the Ministry of Agriculture has said.                        
Speaking in Mogadishu Ministry of Agriculture Yusuf Nur Eid said the ship carrying the consignment left the port of Mogadishu for the international market this week. This is the third consignment since Somalia resumed banana export last year.
	
Nur said the government was finalizing policies and regulatory frameworks to revive the banana sector in the country.
	
            
	
	
    Speaking in Mogadishu Ministry of Agriculture Yusuf Nur Eid said the ship carrying the consignment left the port of Mogadishu for the international market this week. This is the third consignment since Somalia resumed banana export last year.
Nur said the government was finalizing policies and regulatory frameworks to revive the banana sector in the country.
"We are finalizing the policies necessary to revive the Banana Marketing Agency to boost our exports to the international market. The agency will be unveiled soon,” said Nur.
The USAID’s Growth, Enterprise, Employment and Livelihoods (GEEL) has been working with the Ministry of Agriculture and farmers to revive various agricultural and fishing sectors in the country.
(Source: Hiiraan Online)

Senator Moye Partners with Doctors Without Borders -To Provide Free Medical Services to Bong Citizens
MONROVIA – The Chairman of the Bong County Legislative Caucus, Senator Prince Kermue Moye, has partnered with the Liberia Physicians and Surgeons without Borders and its partners from Spain to provide free medical and surgical operations to hundreds of citizens in Bong County.
Citizens experiencing various medical complications would be thoroughly screened and treated by 11 Spanish doctors along with their Liberian counterparts at various health facilities in the county.
The initiative was launched by Senator Moye and others at a local hotel in Paynesville, outside Monrovia on Wednesday, April 2.
Speaking during the launch of the initiative, Senator Prince Moye pointed out that the initiative was intended to buttress the government’s efforts in providing healthcare delivery to its citizens.
He said the cancellation of United States Agency for International Development’s (USAID) support to critical sectors in Liberia by the administration of President Donald Trump has affected most of the country’s health programs.
He noted that as a result of this, Liberia now needs partners like Doctors without Borders who would fill in the gap to guarantee the health and wellbeing of its citizens, adding that, “this partnership is one of such that all of us feel proud and we are so appreciative.”
Senator Moye emphasized that citizens from other counties residing in Bong will also benefit from the treatment.
“This is not your first time. We want to say thank you for coming and we cherish this partnership. This should not be the end. The team from the Executive and Legislature will continue to put small resources together to enhance your work and impact our people positively.”
According to him, healthcare delivery remains paramount to Liberia and its citizens.
“What we have been charged as a people is to always seek assistance for the betterment of our citizens. That will be one of our expectations. This is not going to be the end because we have explored opportunities for our citizens in different fields and this is just coming at the time it is much needed. We hope that those that have been screened and ready to go through the operations and medical care will be successful.”
He further expressed the hope that the treatment of the citizens would enable them to contribute to the county and country rebuilding processes in their different capacities as teachers, nurses, and other disciplines.
“Once they are healthy, they will return to their different communities and provide services to the needy in those communities.”
Senator Moye, however, vowed to continue to work to positively impact the lives of his constituents.
He encouraged sons and daughters hailing from Bong to put aside their differences and rally around one another to help improve the living conditions of their people and move the county and Liberia in general forward.
For her part, Liberia’s Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Dr. Catherine Thomas Cooper recounted the partnership between the Liberian government and the Doctors Without Borders.
She observed that the return of the group to Liberia would not only benefit those seeking medical and surgical operations, but also health workers, including Liberian doctors and nurses.
She said skills would be transferred from the visiting Spanish doctors onto their Liberian counterparts to enhance their profession.
Dr. Cooper stressed that many of the patients across the country are financially constrained to seek adequate healthcare delivery and as such, the free medical and surgical operations of the Doctors Without Borders is a welcoming venture.
“We want to express our sincere gratitude for selecting Liberia as a country where you can provide expert services to our people. We are so grateful and we know that you have been where before and we treasure this partnership. We know that our health workers will benefit from your experience.”
She maintained that the provision of proper care is expensive, and as such, many of those in leeward areas are the ones most often challenged.
She stated that the mission of the Spanish Doctors to Liberia “will really provide support to those patients who cannot afford and otherwise.”
“I’m so happy today that you (Spanish doctors) have accepted to be in Liberia and left your comfort zone to come and serve our people and you are starting from Bong County. Today it is Bong, your next trip will be to another county until you tour the whole Liberia,” the Deputy Minister for Administration at the Ministry of Health Martha Morris stated.
Also speaking, the Team Leader and General Surgeon Antonio Satorra assured that the team will do “a big job” that would save lives in Liberia.
He disclosed that the team will carry out surgical operations on more than 100 patients in Bong.
He expressed gratitude for the reception and level of support his team continues to receive from Senator Moye and other eminent citizens of the county, noting that, “we will start as soon as possible and we will do as much as we can.”

a564.t:
Dans la journée du dimanche 5 novembre 2023 au Sheraton Hôtel, a été organisée une cérémonie de lancement officiel d’un projet d’emploi des jeunes à Djibouti. Une étape importante pour répondre à une priorité nationale. Cette nouvelle initiative de l’USAID, d’une valeur de 16 millions de dollars, renforcera les programmes de main-d’œuvre et créera des opportunités d’emploi durable pour la jeunesse Djiboutienne. Ce projet, qui se déroule de 2023 à 2027, est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’USAID, le ministère du Travail chargé de la réforme de l’administration et de la protection sociale, le ministère de l’Education nationale et de la formation professionnelle et la Chambre de Commerce de Djibouti. Le projet sera mis en œuvre par un consortium entre EDC (Education Development Center) et IESC (Improving Economies for Stronger Communities).
Le projet de USAID/ Djibouti sur l’emploi des jeunes améliorera l’emploi des jeunes Djiboutiens en renforçant les programmes de main-d’œuvre et en créant des emplois durables. Le projet se concentre sur le placement permanent des jeunes Djiboutiens dans des emplois intéressants. Pour atteindre cet objectif, l’initiative encourage l’engagement du secteur privé en collaborant avec des entreprises privées Djiboutiennes, américaines et internationales. En partenariat étroit avec le gouvernement de Djibouti, ce projet de l’USAID est adapté aux dynamiques actuelles du marché. Il s’engage à améliorer la préparation à l’emploi des jeunes Djiboutiens et à accroître leur accès à des opportunités d’emploi de haute qualité. En développant l’implication du secteur privé et en promouvant l’emploi durable, le projet cherche à avoir un impact positif sur la vie des jeunes à Djibouti, contribuant ainsi à la croissance économique et au développement de la nation.
Ce fait d’importance a réuni le ministre de l’Education Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle, Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, le ministre du Travail Chargé de la Formalisation et de la Protection sociale, Omar Abdi Said, le Chargé d’Affaires de l’Ambassade américaine à Djibouti, M.Christopher Snipes, le Président de la Chambre de Commerce de Djibouti, Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, la Vice-présidente et Directrice de la Stratégie des Programmes de la Division du Développement International EDC, Mme Helen Boyle, le Directeur de général de l’ANEFIP, M. Mahamoud Omar, la directrice en charge de la formation au sein de la mission de l’USAID à Djibouti, Mme Zahra Youssouf, des dirigeants d’entreprises.
Après avoir visionner le témoignage vidéo de deux jeunes bénéficiaires de l’ancien programme de l’USAID sur l’employabilité de la main-d’œuvre Djiboutienne (PED-2022), les participants ont écouté précieusement les discours des officiels. Dans une allocution faite à l’endroit de la cérémonie, la vice-présidente et directrice de la stratégie des programmes de la division du développement international, Mme Helen Boyle, a assuré que le consortium EDC et IESC est heureux de constater que le gouvernement de Djibouti et la Mission de l’USAID à Djibouti considèrent l’emploi des jeunes comme l’une des priorités de développement économique et social du pays. « Nous croyons en la création des opportunités d’emploi tout au long de la vie pour les jeunes hommes et femmes » a-t-elle mobilisé. Selon Mme Helen Boyle l’intérêt du gouvernement de Djibouti a été démontré à travers l’engagement des représentants du MENFOP de l’ANEFIP et de la Chambre de Commerce de Djibouti au processus participatif de la Co création ayant permis d’appréhender les réalités de l’écosystème du marché, d’identifier les besoins spécifiques des jeunes vulnérables et de produire le plan d’actions de mise en œuvre de la première année de l’activité.
Pour le ministre de l’Education Nationale et de la Formation Professionnelle, qui prenant la parole à son tour, a indiqué que la mise en synergie des efforts constitués est essentielle pour la réussite de ce projet.
« La conjugaison de nos expériences et expériences dans le domaine du développement de la main d’œuvre est un atout précieux » a-t-il souligné. Le ministre de l’éducation nationale confirme son entière disposition afin de travailler en étroite collaboration avec tout au long de ce projet et qu’il est faudrait créer un écosystème favorable à la formation professionnelle et à l’emploi des jeunes.
Dans son discours à la cérémonie de lancement officiel de l’activité de l’USAID pour l’emploi des jeunes à Djibouti, le ministre du Travail, Chargé de la Formalisation et de la protection sociale, M. Omar Abdi Said a rappelé que la jeunesse Djiboutienne, à l’instar de toutes les jeunesses du monde, fait face à des nombreux défis liés au développement de son potentiel, à une formation adaptée aux exigences et à l’accès au marché du travail, à l’accès aux financements pour ceux qui prennent l’initiative de l’auto entreprenariat. Le ministre du travail a dans ses propos témoigné que le Chef de l’Etat, Son Excellence Ismail Omar Guelleh, a pris l’engagement d’apporter une réponse à cette contrainte, à travers l’action du gouvernement. Selon le ministre du travail cette réponse se veut inclusive, concrète, résiliente dans le terme et surtout efficiente quant aux efforts consenties par l’ensemble des parties prenantes œuvrant dans ce sens a-t-il appuyé.
Quant au président de la Chambre de Commerce, M. Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, a expliqué qu’il est confiant en ce projet qui permettra de renforcer les acquis et atteindre les nouveaux objectifs fixés. Le président de la chambre de commerce affirme qu’axer cette fois-ci sur un appui au secteur privé, le projet est en phase avec les missions de la chambre de commerce. Pour le président de la chambre de commerce, à travers le Centre de Gestion Agréé de son institution, les entreprises sont accompagnées dans la gestion et le conseil et pourront bénéficier d’un renforcement de capacités dans la détermination et la formulation de leurs besoins en matière de Ressources Humaines. Il complète cette étude complété par l’étude réalisée, cela permettra d’avoir In Fine une projection réaliste des besoins en main d’œuvre qualifiée de ces entreprises.
Pour sa part la directrice en charge de la formation au sein de la mission de l’USAID à Djibouti Mme Zahra Youssouf a fait la présentation du sommaire des activités de la période d’inscription du mois d’avril à septembre de l’année 2023.
Également et durant le déroulement de cette journée, ont été des témoignages de quelques dirigeants d’entreprises ayant pris l’engagement de collaborer autour de l’emploi des jeunes avec les partenaires institutionnels et l’activité de l’USAID. La cérémonie s’est soldée par la photo de famille des officiels avec les participants.
Djibril Abdi Ali
a564.en:
Launch ceremony of the USAID project for youth employment in Djibouti

On Sunday 5 November 2023 at the Sheraton Hotel, an official launch ceremony was held for a youth employment project in Djibouti. An important step in responding to a national priority. This new USAID initiative, worth 16 million dollars, will strengthen workforce programmes and create sustainable employment opportunities for Djiboutian youth. This project, which runs from 2023 to 2027, is the fruit of a collaboration between USAID, the Ministry of Labour in charge of administrative reform and social protection, the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training, and the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce. The project will be implemented by a consortium between EDC (Education Development Center) and IESC (Improving Economies for Stronger Communities).

The USAID/Djibouti youth employment project will improve the employment of young Djiboutians by strengthening workforce programmes and creating sustainable jobs. The project focuses on the permanent placement of young Djiboutians in worthwhile jobs. To achieve this objective, the initiative encourages private sector engagement by collaborating with Djiboutian, American and international private companies. In close partnership with the government of Djibouti, this USAID project is adapted to current market dynamics. It is committed to improving the job readiness of young Djiboutians and to increasing their access to high-quality employment opportunities. By developing private sector involvement and promoting sustainable employment, the project seeks to have a positive impact on the lives of young people in Djibouti, thereby contributing to the economic growth and development of the nation.

This important event brought together the Minister of National Education and Vocational Training, Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud; the Minister of Labour in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection, Omar Abdi Said; the Chargé d'Affaires of the American Embassy in Djibouti, Mr Christopher Snipes; the President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce, Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh; the Vice-President and Director of Programme Strategy of the International Development Division of EDC, Mrs Helen Boyle; the Director General of ANEFIP, Mr Mahamoud Omar; the director in charge of training within the USAID mission in Djibouti, Mrs Zahra Youssouf; and business leaders.

After viewing the video testimony of two young beneficiaries of the former USAID programme on the employability of the Djiboutian workforce (PED-2022), the participants listened attentively to the speeches of the officials. In an address delivered to the ceremony, the Vice-President and Director of Programme Strategy of the International Development Division, Mrs Helen Boyle, affirmed that the EDC and IESC consortium is happy to note that the government of Djibouti and the USAID Mission in Djibouti consider youth employment to be one of the country's economic and social development priorities. "We believe in creating lifelong employment opportunities for young men and women," she urged. According to Mrs Helen Boyle, the interest of the government of Djibouti was demonstrated through the commitment of the representatives of MENFOP, ANEFIP and the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce to the participatory co-creation process, which made it possible to grasp the realities of the market ecosystem, to identify the specific needs of vulnerable young people and to produce the implementation action plan for the first year of the activity.

The Minister of National Education and Vocational Training, taking the floor in his turn, indicated that bringing together the assembled efforts is essential to the success of this project.

"The combination of our experiences and expertise in the field of workforce development is a precious asset," he stressed. The Minister of National Education confirmed his full willingness to work in close collaboration throughout this project and said that it would be necessary to create an environment favourable to vocational training and youth employment.

In his speech at the official launch ceremony of the USAID activity for youth employment in Djibouti, the Minister of Labour in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection, Mr Omar Abdi Said, recalled that Djiboutian youth, like all the youth of the world, face many challenges linked to developing their potential, to training adapted to requirements and access to the labour market, and to access to financing for those who take the initiative of self-entrepreneurship. In his remarks, the Minister of Labour testified that the Head of State, His Excellency Ismail Omar Guelleh, has made a commitment to provide a response to this constraint through government action. According to the Minister of Labour, this response is intended to be inclusive, concrete, resilient in the long term and above all efficient with regard to the efforts made by all the stakeholders working in that direction, he stressed.

As for the President of the Chamber of Commerce, Mr Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, he explained that he is confident in this project, which will make it possible to consolidate the gains and reach the new objectives set. The President of the Chamber of Commerce affirms that by focusing this time on support to the private sector, the project is in line with the missions of the chamber of commerce. For the President of the Chamber of Commerce, through his institution's Approved Management Centre, companies are supported in management and advice and will be able to benefit from capacity building in determining and formulating their human resources needs. He adds that this study, complemented by the study carried out, will ultimately make it possible to have a realistic projection of these companies' needs for qualified labour.

For her part, the director in charge of training within the USAID mission in Djibouti, Mrs Zahra Youssouf, presented the summary of activities for the enrolment period from April to September 2023.

Also, during the course of the day, there were testimonies from some business leaders who have committed to collaborating on youth employment with the institutional partners and the USAID activity. The ceremony ended with a family photo of the officials with the participants.

Djibril Abdi Ali

a712.t:
Presidential Adviser on Religious Affairs Rev. Brian Kamwendo and the National Economic Empowerment Fund (NEEF) are standing by their claim that 5,300 clerics have benefitted from K8.3 billion in loans—despite major religious umbrella bodies distancing themselves from the scheme.
Speaking in an interview last evening, Kamwendo shrugged off the growing skepticism from Malawi’s top religious institutions, saying the loans were deliberately targeted at “fraternal clerics” under a pilot phase of the Faith Leaders Empowerment Scheme, not through official church channels.
“We started with the fraternal because this was just a pilot phase with an expectation that we will later engage the mother bodies. So, it is not strange that they don’t know who have benefitted,” Kamwendo explained.
Echoing his remarks, NEEF credit manager Whyghtone Mweta clarified that the clerics accessed the funds after forming groups, and were engaged in various businesses like grocery shops, farming, and mobile money services.
“They are part of the broader ecosystem of Malawian entrepreneurs. We treat them as any eligible Malawian who can benefit from Neef loans,” said Mweta.
But the explanation has done little to quell concerns from the country’s main religious institutions.
The Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB), the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC), and the Muslim Association of Malawi (MAM) have all publicly distanced themselves from Kamwendo’s announcement made during the July 5 national worship service marking Malawi’s 61st independence anniversary.
MCCB general secretary Fr. Valeriano Mtseka said he was unaware of any Catholic cleric—bishop or priest—who had benefitted from the loans.
MCC board chairperson Rev. Billy Gama, whose council comprises 21 denominations, was equally stunned. “Actually, I was right there at the prayers and I was shocked when I heard that statement. To the best of my knowledge, no one [from MCC] has benefitted. It might have been a political statement,” Gama said.
MAM spokesperson Sheikh Dinala Chabulika said his association moved quickly to verify Kamwendo’s claims—only to find “zero” beneficiaries among its members.
“Write [the story] and tell them [government] that we [MAM] haven’t found anyone [who received Neef loans],” said Chabulika.
The confusion comes barely two weeks after Neef refuted a separate report alleging that K5.8 billion was disbursed to just 11 pastors under a purported presidential initiative—raising further questions about transparency and targeting.
Neef, which rebranded in 2020 as an economic empowerment vehicle, said earlier this year it aimed to disburse K150 billion to over 400,000 farmers and entrepreneurs by March 2025. By January this year, the fund had already disbursed K184 billion, reaching over 200,000 Malawians.
Still, the current saga underscores a deeper issue: a glaring communication gap between government initiatives and the very institutions expected to anchor trust among faith-based communities.

a770.t:
Harare, (New Ziana) -The Zimbabwe government is in the process of procuring 80 combine harvesters from Belarus, bringing the total number of the machines to around 400 against a national demand of 600, a senior official has said.
Deputy director in the Department of Agriculture Engineering, Mechanisation and Farm Infrastructure Development Harrison Bhasikoro said this in an interview with New Ziana on the harvesting preparedness for the summer cropping season.
He said the country is expecting a bumper harvest and the government wants to ensure a seamless harvesting process for farmers across the country.
“Obviously the country is expecting a bumper harvest, so in as far as taking out the crop from the fields, that is harvesting of the crop, I think also as a country we are prepared to do that, especially when we are looking at combine harvesting services,” he said, adding that currently the country has 313 combine harvesters.
Bhasikoro said with each combine able to harvest at least 10 hectares per day, their capacity to harvest the 2024/25 summer crop will be around 4 000 hectares per day.
“So if we consider a 150-day harvesting, then our minimum capacity will be close to 700 000 hectares. So as a country we are prepared in as far as combine harvester services is concerned. “
It’s not like all farmers will request combine harvester services, but also some farmers will do shelling and thrashing, so from the study that we carried out, as a country we are also prepared in as far as thrashing and shelling services are concerned,” he said.
He said the country has enough equipment both from the government and private players to provide thrashing and shelling services. He encouraged farmers who have not arranged for harvesting services to approach their offices either at provincial or district level and register.
The government is also working closely with Agriculture Finance Leasing Company as well as the Agricultural and Rural Development Authority (ARDA) and other private entities to assist during the harvesting period, he said.
“So in a nutshell we are saying we are, as a country, prepared to harvest all the crop on time so that also for those who want to switch from summer to winter wheat, also we are putting arrangements on the ground so that we can actually remove the summer crop so that they can quickly switch to winter cropping,” he said.
Bhasikoro said the government is working to achieve the national requirement for combine harvesters of 600 by the end of next year.
New Ziana

a864.t:
Talented artists Young Zesh and Tru Classic made a significant impact on Sunday at the exclusive Show Them Flames Night event held at Hotel Sky in Sandton.
This event was a collaborative initiative between the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC) and AIRCO.
ENCAC Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Stanley Dlamini shared how the event showcased a vibrant array of talent, with Eswatini’s Young Zesh and Tru Classic delivering electrifying performances that earned a standing ovation from a discerning audience.
Also Read: SA company interested in sponsoring Miss Teen
The prestigious event was graced by prominent figures from the South African entertainment industry and key media personalities.
Dlamini noted that the stage was alive with energy from a diverse line-up of performers, including Mthokozisi Ndaba, Yamke, Don Dada, Kingsmen, and the closing act, Aubrey Qwabe. He added that each artist contributed to a memorable evening, celebrating the richness of regional artistic talent.
Celebrating Cross-Border Collaboration
Speaking at the event, AIRCO Deputy Chairperson Stanley Khoza extended heartfelt gratitude to the ENCAC CEO for facilitating this pivotal collaboration.
“This is just the beginning of many more collaborations between our two nations,” Khoza stated, emphasising the strategic importance of cross-border artistic exchange.
Dlamini expressed appreciation for the warm reception accorded to the Eswatini artists and delegation in Sandton. He specifically acknowledged the presence and instrumental role of the Eswatini National Arts and Culture Awards (NACA) Chairperson, the legendary Sipho Makhabane, who was part of the delegation and crucial in making this program a follow-up success to the recent Eswatini Arts Summit.
He reiterated the need for continued collaboration and extended an invitation to South African media to further promote Eswatini talent, highlighting the interconnectedness of the global village.
Studio Collaboration Born from Performance
A key outcome of the event was the immediate collaboration between Young Zesh and South African artist Yamke.
Khoza formally introduced the two artists, confirming that they had entered the studio on Monday to record a collaborative track with a top-tier technical team.
According to Khoza, Show Them Flames will oversee the post-production of the highly-anticipated song, with plans to visit Eswatini for its official launch.

Vendors operating at the Opuwo Information and Cultural Centre have appealed to authorities to improve the centre's infrastructure.
They complained that the current sorry state of the centre was chasing away their clients.
The Opuwo Information and Cultural Centre, known as the Green Building, was established in 2008 and was meant to be a craft centre for the Opuwo Town Council.
They are now calling on the stakeholders to help improve the state of the centre.
The Opuwo Town Council's support officer, Gebhardt Makono, said the town council plans to revamp and improve the centre to attract clients.
However, he was quick to point out that no budget has been allocated yet, as the council is still busy with assessment.

a979.t:
Li Anqi, journaliste du Quotidien du Peuple
Le développement incarne l’aspiration des peuples à une vie meilleure. C’est la priorité absolue des pays en développement et un thème éternel de la société humaine. Le 21 septembre 2021, le président chinois Xi Jinping a solennellement proposé l’Initiative pour le développement mondial lors du débat général de la 76e Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, apportant ainsi la sagesse et la force de la Chine pour résoudre les problèmes de développement mondial. Au cours des trois dernières années, le mécanisme de coopération de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial a été continuellement amélioré et les résultats de la coopération sont devenus de plus en plus fructueux.
Au cours de ces trois dernières années, le « cercle d’amis » de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial s’est de plus en plus élargi ; il compte aujourd’hui le soutien et la participation de plus de 100 pays et de plusieurs organisations internationales, dont les Nations Unies. Plus de 80 pays ont rejoint le « Groupe d’amis » de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial ». Plus de 70 pays, régions et organisations internationales ont établi conjointement un réseau de centres mondiaux de promotion du développement. Plus de 40 pays et organisations internationales ont signé des mémorandums d’accord sur la coopération avec la Chine. Un Groupe de travail sur la promotion de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial a été créé par les Nations Unies, et un Centre de démonstration pour la coopération Chine-Afrique (Éthiopie)-ONU (ONUDI) a été inauguré… La coopération liée à l’Initiative pour le développement mondial ne cesse de s’approfondir et de devenir plus pratique, et a reçu de nombreux éloges et une participation active de la communauté internationale.
L’Initiative pour le développement mondial vient certes de la Chine, mais les occasions et les résultats qu’elle offre appartiennent au monde entier. Depuis que cette initiative a été proposée il y a trois ans, la Chine a pris des mesures pratiques pour enrichir les canaux de financement du développement, innover dans les modèles de coopération au développement, renforcer les capacités de développement, élargir les réseaux de partenaires de développement, coordonner les actions avec toutes les parties et obtenir des résultats à long terme, formant ainsi un partenariat vigoureux pour la promotion du développement durable.
Le dialogue de haut niveau sur le développement mondial qui s’est tenu en juin 2022 marque le début de l’enracinement de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial. Lors du dialogue, la Chine a annoncé des mesures pragmatiques pour mettre en œuvre l’initiative, notamment la transformation du Fonds d’aide à la coopération Sud-Sud en Fonds mondial pour le développement et la coopération Sud-Sud, l’augmentation de la contribution au Fonds d’affectation spéciale pour la paix et le développement des Nations Unies, la création d’un Centre de promotion du développement mondial et d’un Réseau mondial de connaissances pour le développement, et la publication d’un Rapport mondial sur le développement etc.
Le dialogue a également publié une liste de résultats contenant 32 initiatives, dont la création de l’Alliance de partenariat mondial pour la lutte contre la pauvreté et le développement, le lancement de « l’Action spéciale pour promouvoir la production alimentaire », la création de l’Alliance internationale de coopération pour l’innovation et de recherche et développement en matière de vaccins, l’établissement d’un partenariat mondial sur les énergies propres, la création d’un réseau mondial de gestion durable des forêts, l’organisation de forums internationaux sur le développement mondial et la fourniture de 100 000 places de formation et de séminaires aux pays en développement.
Amélioration du « Fonds de développement mondial et de coopération Sud-Sud » et nouvelle augmentation du capital, établissement de manière innovante d’une bibliothèque de projets de développement mondial qui a attiré plus de 1 000 projets ; mise en œuvre de plus de 140 projets de coopération trilatérale dans plus de 60 pays avec plus de 20 organisations internationales ; mise en place d’une base de formation innovante pour le Centre de Promotion du Développement Mondial ; offre d’opportunités de formation aux personnes des pays en développement ; création d’un « Foyer pour les étudiants chinois en formation en aide étrangère » et d’un « Foyer pour les jeunes leaders du développement mondial » ; organisation de plus de 1 000 projets de renforcement des capacités pour les pays en développement et formation de plus de 40 000 talents de tous types… La Chine s’est associée à ses partenaires pour accélérer la mise en œuvre des initiatives de coopération et renforcer continuellement la dynamique du développement mondial.
Selon Stephen Bainous Kargbo, représentant de l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour le développement industriel en Chine, l’Initiative pour le développement mondial a aidé à mobiliser des ressources, à établir des mécanismes de coopération et à faire progresser la coopération pratique, et les grands progrès réalisés dans des domaines tels que la réduction de la pauvreté, la sécurité alimentaire et la santé ont démontré la détermination et la capacité de la Chine à contribuer au bien-être mondial et à la prospérité commune. Carlos Maria Correa, directeur exécutif du South Center, a pour sa part noté que l’Initiative pour le développement mondial s’aligne sur les priorités des pays en développement, en mettant l’accent sur les objectifs de développement durable et en fournissant un soutien plus fort et plus ciblé à ces nations.
Sur la voie du développement et de la prospérité, aucun pays ne peut être laissé pour compte et personne ne peut être oublié. C’est la vision de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial et l’objectif défendu par les Nations Unies. Dennis Francis, président de la 78e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, a souligné que les objectifs de l’Initiative pour le développement mondial sont conformes au Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030 des Nations Unies et ont un grand potentiel pour bénéficier aux pays du monde entier. La vision défendue par l’Initiative incarne l’esprit du véritable multilatéralisme et bâtira un monde plus équitable et plus durable pour tous.
À l’avenir, la Chine approfondira sa coopération avec toutes les parties sur l’Initiative pour le développement mondial, continuera de partager les opportunités de la modernisation chinoise, accélérera la mise en œuvre de l’Agenda 2030 des Nations Unies pour le développement durable et favorisera le développement commun, afin de favoriser un paradigme de développement présentant des avantages pour tous, l’équilibre, la coordination, l’inclusion, la coopération gagnant-gagnant et la prospérité commune, et de créer un avenir encore plus brillant pour l’humanité.
a979.en:
Li Anqi, journalist, People's Daily

Development embodies people's aspiration for a better life. It is the top priority of developing countries and an eternal theme of human society. On 21 September 2021, Chinese President Xi Jinping solemnly proposed the Global Development Initiative during the general debate of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly, thereby bringing China's wisdom and strength to solving global development problems. Over the past three years, the cooperation mechanism of the Global Development Initiative has been continuously improved and the results of cooperation have become increasingly fruitful.

Over these past three years, the "circle of friends" of the Global Development Initiative has expanded more and more; today it counts the support and participation of more than 100 countries and several international organisations, including the United Nations. More than 80 countries have joined the "Group of Friends" of the Global Development Initiative. More than 70 countries, regions and international organisations have jointly established a network of global development promotion centres. More than 40 countries and international organisations have signed memoranda of understanding on cooperation with China. A Working Group on the Promotion of the Global Development Initiative has been created by the United Nations, and a Demonstration Centre for China-Africa (Ethiopia)-UN (UNIDO) cooperation has been inaugurated. Cooperation linked to the Global Development Initiative continues to deepen and become more practical, and has received much praise and active participation from the international community.

The Global Development Initiative certainly comes from China, but the opportunities and results it offers belong to the whole world. Since this initiative was proposed three years ago, China has taken practical steps to enrich development financing channels, innovate development cooperation models, strengthen development capacities, broaden development partner networks, coordinate actions with all parties and obtain long-term results, thus forming a vigorous partnership for the promotion of sustainable development.

The High-level Dialogue on Global Development held in June 2022 marks the beginning of the Global Development Initiative taking root. During the dialogue, China announced pragmatic measures to implement the initiative, in particular transforming the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund into the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund, increasing its contribution to the United Nations Peace and Development Trust Fund, creating a Global Development Promotion Centre and a Global Development Knowledge Network, and publishing a Global Development Report, among others.

The dialogue also released a list of outcomes containing 32 initiatives, including the creation of the Global Partnership Alliance for Poverty Reduction and Development, the launch of the "Special Action to Promote Food Production", the creation of the International Alliance for Vaccine Innovation and Research and Development Cooperation, the establishment of a global clean energy partnership, the creation of a global sustainable forest management network, the organisation of international forums on global development, and the provision of 100,000 training and seminar places to developing countries.

Improvement of the "Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund" and a further capital increase; the innovative establishment of a global development project library which has attracted more than 1,000 projects; implementation of more than 140 trilateral cooperation projects in more than 60 countries with more than 20 international organisations; establishment of an innovative training base for the Global Development Promotion Centre; provision of training opportunities to people from developing countries; creation of a "Home for Chinese students in foreign aid training" and a "Home for young global development leaders"; organisation of more than 1,000 capacity-building projects for developing countries and the training of more than 40,000 talents of all kinds. China has joined with its partners to accelerate the implementation of cooperation initiatives and continuously strengthen the momentum of global development.

According to Stephen Bainous Kargbo, representative of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization in China, the Global Development Initiative has helped mobilise resources, establish cooperation mechanisms and advance practical cooperation, and the great progress achieved in areas such as poverty reduction, food security and health has demonstrated China's determination and capacity to contribute to global well-being and common prosperity. Carlos Maria Correa, executive director of the South Centre, for his part noted that the Global Development Initiative aligns with the priorities of developing countries, emphasising the sustainable development goals and providing stronger and more targeted support to these nations.

On the path of development and prosperity, no country can be left behind and no one can be forgotten. This is the vision of the Global Development Initiative and the objective upheld by the United Nations. Dennis Francis, President of the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly, stressed that the objectives of the Global Development Initiative are consistent with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and have great potential to benefit countries around the world. The vision championed by the Initiative embodies the spirit of true multilateralism and will build a fairer and more sustainable world for all.

In the future, China will deepen its cooperation with all parties on the Global Development Initiative, continue to share the opportunities of Chinese modernisation, accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and promote common development, in order to foster a development paradigm offering benefits for all, balance, coordination, inclusion, win-win cooperation and common prosperity, and to create an even brighter future for humanity.

a1063.t:
O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, condenou o tiroteio perto de um centro de distribuição de ajuda humanitária no sul da Faixa de Gaza, que fez 27 mortos, uma situação que o seu porta-voz descreveu como inconcebível.
“É inaceitável que os civis arrisquem e, por vezes, percam a vida simplesmente à procura de comida”, disse Stéphane Dujarric aos jornalistas, citada por Notícias ao Minuto, reiterando o apelo para uma investigação independente e já exigida após incidentes semelhantes esta semana.
O Exército israelita anunciou que abriu uma investigação depois de a Cruz Vermelha ter confirmado a morte de 27 palestinianos após um tiroteio, ocorrido perto de um centro de distribuição de ajuda humanitária no sul da Faixa de Gaza.
Na manhã de ontem, os soldados israelitas “dispararam tiros de aviso (…) contra suspeitos que se aproximavam de uma forma que colocava a sua segurança em risco”, referiu Effie Defrin, porta-voz do Exército israelita.
“O incidente está sob investigação e vamos esclarecer completamente” o sucedido, acrescentou, indicando que o Exército “não estava a bloquear o acesso dos residentes de Gaza” aos pontos de distribuição de ajuda humanitária.
“Pelo contrário, estamos a permitir. É o Hamas que está a impedir esse acesso”, contrapôs, em referência ao grupo islamita palestiniano que governa o território desde 2007.
O Comité Internacional da Cruz Vermelha (CICV) confirmou a morte de 27 pessoas nos incidentes junto do centro de distribuição de ajuda humanitária, tal como já tinham informado anteriormente as organizações de socorro do território palestiniano.
“Ao início desta manhã, o hospital de campanha da Cruz Vermelha, com 60 camas, em Rafah (sul), recebeu um fluxo massivo de 184 doentes. Dezanove deles foram declarados mortos à chegada, e outros oito sucumbiram aos ferimentos pouco depois. A maioria dos doentes foi baleada”, descreveu o CICV em comunicado.
Os incidentes com tiros tornaram-se quase diários após uma fundação apoiada por Israel e pelos Estados Unidos ter estabelecido pontos de distribuição de ajuda humanitária dentro de zonas militares israelitas, um sistema que, segundo a organização, visa evitar o Hamas.
As Nações Unidas rejeitaram o novo sistema, alegando que não responde à crescente crise de fome no território e permite a Israel utilizar a ajuda humanitária como arma.
A organização em causa, a Fundação Humanitária de Gaza (GHF), nomeou entretanto um pastor evangélico de direita, o reverendo Johnnie Moore, para a sua liderança.
Em comunicado, a entidade privada encarregada desde a semana passada de entregar ajuda humanitária a um único local no sul da Faixa de Gaza anunciou que o reverendo, nomeado comissário para a Liberdade Religiosa Internacional pelo Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, será o seu novo diretor-geral.
a1063.en:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the shooting near a humanitarian aid distribution centre in the south of the Gaza Strip, which left 27 dead, a situation that his spokesperson described as inconceivable.

"It is unacceptable that civilians risk and, at times, lose their lives simply while looking for food," Stephane Dujarric told journalists, quoted by Noticias ao Minuto, reiterating the call for an independent investigation already demanded after similar incidents this week.

The Israeli Army announced that it had opened an investigation after the Red Cross confirmed the death of 27 Palestinians following a shooting that occurred near a humanitarian aid distribution centre in the south of the Gaza Strip.

Yesterday morning, Israeli soldiers "fired warning shots (...) at suspects who were approaching in a manner that put their safety at risk," said Effie Defrin, spokesperson for the Israeli Army.

"The incident is under investigation and we will fully clarify" what happened, he added, indicating that the Army "was not blocking the access of Gaza residents" to the humanitarian aid distribution points.

"On the contrary, we are allowing it. It is Hamas that is preventing that access," he countered, in reference to the Palestinian Islamist group that has governed the territory since 2007.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) confirmed the death of 27 people in the incidents near the humanitarian aid distribution centre, as relief organisations in the Palestinian territory had previously reported.

"Early this morning, the Red Cross's 60-bed field hospital in Rafah (south) received a massive influx of 184 patients. Nineteen of them were declared dead on arrival, and another eight succumbed to their injuries shortly afterwards. The majority of the patients had been shot," the ICRC described in a statement.

Shooting incidents have become almost daily since a foundation backed by Israel and the United States established humanitarian aid distribution points inside Israeli military zones, a system which, according to the organisation, aims to avoid Hamas.

The United Nations rejected the new system, claiming that it does not respond to the growing hunger crisis in the territory and allows Israel to use humanitarian aid as a weapon.

The organisation in question, the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), has meanwhile appointed a right-wing evangelical pastor, the Reverend Johnnie Moore, to its leadership. In a statement, the private entity charged since last week with delivering humanitarian aid to a single location in the south of the Gaza Strip announced that the reverend, appointed commissioner for International Religious Freedom by the President of the United States, Donald Trump, will be its new director-general.

a1116.t:
Entre le 25 et le 31 mai 2025, quelque 300 migrants ont été interceptés en Méditerranée centrale puis ramenés sur les côtes libyennes, a rapporté l’Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM).
L’interception, en une semaine, de 300 migrants en haute mer sur les côtes libyennes illustre l’ancrage d’une crise migratoire persistante sur cette route maritime périlleuse reliant l’Afrique du Nord à l’Europe.
Les opérations ont été menées au large de plusieurs villes côtières libyennes – Zuwara, Sabratha, Azzawiya, Tripoli et Al-Khums – qui figurent parmi les principaux points de départ des embarcations de migrants.
Depuis le début de l’année, l’OIM recense 9 585 migrants reconduits en Libye, dont 8 147 hommes, 960 femmes et 333 enfants. Parmi eux, 145 étaient des mineurs non accompagnés ou des personnes nécessitant une assistance particulière.
À la date du 31 mai 2025, au moins 233 migrants ont perdu la vie en mer, tandis que 225 autres sont portés disparus.
Malgré les dangers et les critiques sur les conditions d’accueil en Libye, les tentatives de traversée se poursuivent. En 2024, 21 762 migrants avaient été interceptés, avec un bilan de 665 morts et 1 034 disparus. L’année précédente, on dénombrait 962 décès et 1 536 disparitions en mer.
L’OIM réitère que la Libye ne peut être considérée comme un port sûr pour le débarquement des migrants. L’organisation précise ne pas être impliquée dans les opérations d’interception, mais fournit une aide humanitaire à l’arrivée, tout en appelant à des alternatives durables et respectueuses des droits fondamentaux.
SL/te/Sf/APA
a1116.en:
Libya: 300 migrants intercepted at sea, returned in 7 days (IOM)

Between 25 and 31 May 2025, some 300 migrants were intercepted in the central Mediterranean and then brought back to the Libyan coast, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported.
The interception, in one week, of 300 migrants on the high seas off the Libyan coast illustrates the entrenchment of a persistent migration crisis on this perilous maritime route linking North Africa to Europe.
The operations were carried out off several Libyan coastal cities – Zuwara, Sabratha, Azzawiya, Tripoli and Al-Khums – which are among the main departure points for migrant boats.
Since the beginning of the year, the IOM has counted 9,585 migrants returned to Libya, including 8,147 men, 960 women and 333 children. Among them, 145 were unaccompanied minors or people requiring special assistance.
As of 31 May 2025, at least 233 migrants had lost their lives at sea, while 225 others are reported missing.
Despite the dangers and the criticism over reception conditions in Libya, attempts to cross continue. In 2024, 21,762 migrants had been intercepted, with a toll of 665 dead and 1,034 missing. The previous year, there were 962 deaths and 1,536 disappearances at sea.
The IOM reiterates that Libya cannot be considered a safe port for the disembarkation of migrants. The organisation states that it is not involved in the interception operations, but provides humanitarian assistance on arrival, while calling for sustainable alternatives that respect fundamental rights.
SL/te/Sf/APA

a1248.t:
The top judge in the United States has given temporary backing to the Trump administration’s freeze on foreign aid payments.
Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts’ intervention came as the administration faced a midnight deadline (05:00 GMT on Thursday) to pay contractors.
Officials had argued that they could not process the payments within the timeframe set by a lower court judge.
Since coming to power in January, US President Donald Trump has taken quick action to end many aid programmes, largely run by the US Agency for International Development, USAID, and placed most of its staff on administrative leave or sacked them.
The Trump administration is seeking to shrink the federal workforce and cut costs in a drive led by Elon Musk.
The billionaire Trump adviser asked millions of bureaucrats over the weekend to list their accomplishments from the past week – sparking fury amongst the workforce and disagreement with officials leading the departments.
US District Judge Amir Ali had ordered the US State Department and USAID to pay about $2bn-worth of bills (£1.6bn) to contractors by midnight on Wednesday.
It is one of many interventions by judges trying to stop or pause a wave of Trump administration orders.
As the deadline approached, the Trump administration went to the Supreme Court, arguing it was impossible to process claims in an orderly fashion in such a short period of time.
The US federal government freeze comes as the administration carries out a review of foreign aid funding.
Credit: bbc.com

a1365.t:
A critical review of Tanzania’s Development Vision (TDV) 2050 points to risks to its success where previous development policies have failed. It is worth noting that Tanzania has consistently missed development targets since independence, despite various policy approaches.
The current vision acknowledges key issues including persistent poverty, the dominance of the informal economy, and the failure to process raw materials like cashews as some of the main bottlenecks for economic transformation in the country.
Vision 2050 sets the ambitious target of turning Tanzania into a trillion-dollar economy from the current baseline of US$86 billion driven primarily by the private sector and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), with the government transitioning to an enabler of business.
The first pillar
The first pillar of the vision targets a strong, inclusive and competitive economy built on macroeconomic stability and predictability, fiscal sustainability, innovative and diversified financing. It identifies as key drivers of this economy an enabling business and investment environment, efficient state-owned enterprises, a vibrant private sector and strategic regional and global opportunities.
It is important to point out that Tanzania is far from being a truly market-driven economy, with a proliferation of state-owned enterprises and regulatory bodies. It is also important to question the effectiveness of Foreign Direct Investment in priority sectors like mining, which has historically led to exclusion of Tanzanians in participating in their own economy, inequality and limited job creation.
READ MORE: President Samia Unveils Vision 2050, Urges Focus on Implementation
When the state has engaged in real estate, it is often linked to speculative investments and rent-seeking. Equally critical is the failure to implement agricultural policy goals, such as modernisation and commercialisation which is partly due to collaboration between officials and business interests to compromise stated policy objectives.
It is imperative that the policy conditions promote transparency and accountability among key actors in ways that reinforce trust between the state, the market and society towards the shared objective of a truly competitive and inclusive economy.
The second pillar
The second pillar, on Human Capabilities and Social Development, aims to enhance human capital and create an inclusive, healthy society through education, health, social protection, housing, workforce development, and social cohesion. While the aspirations are commendable, the plan lacks specifics on how to overcome challenges, particularly Tanzania’s rapidly growing population, which exacerbates issues across all subsections.
It is worth noting the contradictions with the current administration’s policies, such as the failure to prevent pregnant girls from being expelled from school as provided for under the 2002 Education Regulations despite pledges for sexual and reproductive health education.
Notwithstanding, there is considerable room to build on some of the registered advancements achieved including the increased availability of essential health commodities, strategic investments in water infrastructure facilitated by the Tanzania Water Investment Programme (TanWIP), and concerted efforts to improve the labour force through the establishment of Special Economic Zones and vocational training initiatives.
READ MORE: Media Stakeholders Call for Legal Protection of Vision 2050
To realise the full potential of such gains would require concerted efforts by both the state and non-state actors to mobilise resources towards addressing the most pressing social development problems of our time. Running a successful social protection sector whether via universal health care or national health insurance requires transparency from the state if citizens are to trust and invest in them.
TDV 2050 acknowledges how communities are making significant investment in building social safety nets but it fails to acknowledge how the success of these is based on the significant mutual trust built between their memberships and communities.
A 2014 study identified the lack of fairness, competence and neutrality of governance players as contributing to citizens not trusting in public parastatals in Tanzania, which could significantly hamper attempts to build a viable social protection economy.
The third pillar
The third pillar on Environmental Integrity and Climate Change Resilience acknowledges Tanzania’s susceptibility to climate change and delineates ambitious environmental objectives across five domains: biodiversity, wetlands and water resources, environmental pollution, land management, and climate change resilience.
Nevertheless, these aspirations are undermined by the underlying extractivist economic ambitions, particularly the rapid expansion of fossil fuel extraction, mining, and large-scale industrial agriculture.
READ MORE: Empowering Tanzania: Vision 2050 and The Blueprint For a Fair and Inclusive Prosperity
The stated emphasis on increasing “high value market-oriented produce” in agriculture carries risks of long-term soil degradation and compromises food sovereignty. Reliance on liquefied natural gas (LNG) as an economic catalyst, despite being presented as a “bridge fuel,” risks entrenching further dependence on fossil fuels while posing risks of environmental degradation.
The absence of a clear commitment to a Just Energy Transition in the plan is a significant omission that undermines the credibility of the Vision’s climate commitments. Achieving the ambitions set out in the third pillar of the vision, it is necessary to address inherent tensions between economic growth and sustainability.
As such, its transformative potential will hinge upon the navigation and resolution of these contradictions during implementation.
Beyond the three pillars, it is critical to reflect on the current governance and political atmosphere which make achieving significant change under Vision 2050 unlikely.
Reforms needed
Achieving the enormous public and private investment targets to propel the country’s economic growth to the desired 10 per cent annually requires vivid reforms of the investment environment as well evident independence of key governance institutions, including the judiciary.
READ MORE: Committee for Drafting Tanzania Vision 2050 Revealed
Ranking 96th out of 142 countries globally and 11th out of 34 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Tanzania requires considerable investment in key institutions of accountability. according to the World Justice Project. The anticipated rapid expansion of social services as articulated under Pillar 2 would be hard to achieve in the absence of strong local government authorities that have the capacity to raise their own revenue towards strategic investment.
It would also require massive improvement in social accountability which thrives in an environment where there is notable freedom of expression to allow citizens to claim accountability for delivering results at the local level.
TDV 2050 recognises a declining freedom of expression in Tanzania but falls short of outlining the key measures to reinstate and guarantee such freedom, noting that: “‘Freedom of expression remains constrained and has yet to meet societal expectations. The media space is limited, and professional and structural issues hinder open discourse.’ ‘Although the government has undertaken various efforts, corruption remains a persistent barrier hindering the realisation of social justice and inclusive development.”
Untangling this constrained environment is key to unleashing the potential outlined in the vision.
Public accountability
Ultimately, success in implementing the vision rests on robust public accountability. At one time, Tanzania had a robust infrastructure for such accountability through the Public Expenditure Review which brought together government, civil society, private sector and development practitioners to take stock of progress, identify bottlenecks and deliberate on pathways for improved development outcomes under the aegis of Vision 2025.
Similar arrangements can certainly be replicated in the context of TDV 2050 and civil society stands a unique opportunity to self-organise towards such a public accountability forum for the implementation of TDV 2050.
Doing so, however, would require a relatively free and open research environment to allow for independent monitoring and verification of reported development outcomes so non-state actors contribute meaningfully to such a process.
Writing the vision is a good first step but realising its ambitious goals requires an unrelenting commitment to accountability and honest dialogue about the dire state of governance currently prevalent in Tanzania.
Martin Hockey is an International Law and Human Rights fellow at Center for Strategic Litigation. He’s available at marty@strategiclawcentre.org.
Benjamin Foster is a Climate Justice Fellow under the Queen Elizabeth Scholars Fellowship 2025 at the Transnational Justice Clinic at McGill University currently hosted at the Center for Strategic Litigation. He’s available at ben@strategiclawcentre.org.
Brian Cooksey is a renowned governance and development advisor who currently serves as Research Advisor at Center for Strategic Litigation. He’s available brian@strategiclawcentre.org.
Deus Valentine Rweyemamu is the Chief Executive Officer of the Center for Strategic Litigation. He’s available at deus@strategiclawcentre.org.
